subject: Animation
title: Render Farms: The Computers Behind CGI
description: A 60-second lesson on Render Farms: The Computers Behind CGI.

hook.text: A render farm is a warehouse full of thousands of computers working together to generate CGI animation frames.

buildup.text: Each frame of a CGI film must be rendered — computed pixel by pixel from 3D scene data into a final image.

discovery.text: Disney's render farm has over 55,000 cores processing frames simultaneously around the clock.

twist.text: Despite all that power, complex scenes in films like Moana still took over 100 hours per frame to render.

climax.text: Render farms are the hidden industrial backbone that makes every CGI animated film physically possible.

punchline.text: 55,000 computer cores work for days to produce one second of animation.

quiz.question: What is a render farm in CGI animation?
options: A studio where artists draw animation frames by hand
A warehouse of thousands of computers that process 3D scene data into final animation frames
A software program that edits completed animation

details.summary: Render farms are massive clusters of computers that process the final images of CGI animation. A single Pixar frame can take 24 hours to render, requiring thousands of machines working simultaneously to complete a film.
details.whyItMatters: Render farms are the hidden infrastructure that makes modern animated films possible. Without enormous computational power, the detailed lighting, textures, and effects audiences expect simply could not be produced.
takeaways: Render farms use thousands of computers to process animation frames
A single complex frame can take many hours to render
Computational power directly limits animation visual quality

faq.question: How powerful are the render farms at major animation studios?
faq.answer: Pixar's render farm has over 2,000 machines. For Monsters University, they rendered over 29 hours per frame on average. Major studios collectively use computing power rivaling scientific supercomputer installations.

faq.question: Why does rendering take so long for animation?
faq.answer: Each pixel requires calculating light bouncing between surfaces, transparent materials, subsurface scattering in skin, hair strand reflections, and environmental effects. Realistic light simulation is computationally enormous.
